steps.action: Upload a .docx with Placeholders, one directive, and one Block with Upload version
steps.actual: Dialog caption read "Each upload adds a file version. A new Placeholder gets a form field; a removed one leaves its field in place.". After Upload the dialog reported "File version 1: 8 Placeholders, 1 Block. 6 form fields created." and closed with Close.

steps.action: Read the template pane: every Placeholder and Block is marked, including header, footer, and footnote
steps.actual: Pane heading shows the filename with pill "File version 1" and summary "8 Placeholders, 1 Block". Chips: ["{{counterparty_name}}","{{signing_date}}","{{fee_amount|currency:USD}}","{{governing_law}}","{{arbitration_seat}}","{{reference_code}}","{{counterparty_name}}","{{counterparty_name}}"]. steps.action: A directive decides the new field's type: currency directive created a Currency field, others Text

steps.action: Select a field from its chip and edit the label, type, and help from its card; the form follows each commit

observations: The guide's 'file on the left and its form on the right' describes the desktop layout only; at 390 px the form stacks under the file. Not a defect, but the sentence could say 'beside' or note narrow screens.
The pane lists the Header section after Footer and Footnotes. Fields for Placeholders that exist only in a header, footer, or footnote are appended after every body field.
Keyboard: activating a chip selects its field and opens the card, but focus stays on the chip; reaching the card's inputs needs many further Tab presses.
At 390 px the Upload version button label is clipped by about 13 px in the pane header and the record title truncates to a few characters. The control still works.
The Help copy carries a 'Validation in progress' badge because the catalog status is review.
previousAttempt: A first run on 2026-09-16 (records DOC-028 * 1789551331157) passed every product check but the reviewer's own Help-link check read the record page heading before the lazily loaded Help route rendered, and the keyboard check depended on it. Both checks were rewritten to wait for the article heading and to start from the Form section; the second run (this record) passed all checks. The first run's records remain in the lab as fictional DOC-028 records.
limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.
Both roles ran the same scripted procedure; the Administrator ran the supplementary two-directives check in a separate Auto-Doc.
Slug length and character rules were checked against source only, not exercised in the browser.
Help contrast was seen in the default theme only; the Warm and Dark themes were not checked.
Keyboard and narrow-layout checks are measurements by the reviewer's script, not a screen-reader session.
The lab is shared with other automated journeys; only records named DOC-028 * and the one invited member were created by this walkthrough. Nothing was deleted or reconfigured.
